expectations.text: Normalizes the ROAS units before comparing: mobile-UA tooling reports a percentage, web platforms report a multiplier
expectations.evidence: "Mobile UA tooling typically reports ROAS as a percentage where 100% = breakeven (revenue equals spend). Web/ecommerce platforms report ROAS as a multiplier where 1x = breakeven."

expectations.text: Converts 160% to 1.6x and compares like units (making the web store's 4.2x materially ahead on reported figures)
expectations.evidence: Table converts App 160% → 1.6x and Web 4.2x → 420%, then states "Normalized honestly, web is still ahead — 4.2x vs 1.6x, not a 100x misread."

expectations.text: Warns that comparing the two conventions raw produces a large misread
expectations.evidence: "Normalized honestly, web is still ahead — 4.2x vs 1.6x, not a 100x misread." — this explicitly flags that a raw (unnormalized) comparison would produce a large (100x-scale) misread.

expectations.text: Treats adopting Performance Max as delegating the bidding policy to the platform, not as a campaign-type checkbox
expectations.evidence: "PMax is a delegated bidding archetype, not a targeting option layered on top of your existing strategy. Turning it on **is** the bid-strategy decision — it hands the platform your optimization objective, targeting, creative selection, and placement jointly."

expectations.text: Notes AI-default campaign types use automated bidding exclusively, so adoption is itself the bid-strategy decision
expectations.evidence: "Turning it on **is** the bid-strategy decision — it hands the platform your optimization objective, targeting, creative selection, and placement jointly. There is no 'flip it on and see' version of this that isn't also 'hand over the wheel and see.'" The transcript ties adoption directly to being the bid-strategy decision, though it doesn't explicitly state PMax "uses automated bidding exclusively" as a categorical fact about AI-default campaign types generally.

expectations.text: Asks or answers what signal the platform gets under the delegation
expectations.evidence: "**What signal does the platform get?** PMax bids on whatever conversion event and values you feed it. Given that web's own ROAS number isn't yet confirmed as incremental or margin-checked (see Q1), feeding an unverified/undifferentiated value signal into a fully automated bidder means PMax will optimize hard toward a number you don't yet trust."

expectations.text: Asks or answers what control is given up by delegating
expectations.evidence: "**What control does delegating give up?** Search-term visibility, placement-level attribution, and the ability to isolate what's actually driving results — all reduced."

expectations.text: Requires a written exit criterion: what would justify taking control back
expectations.evidence: "**What would justify taking it back?** If you can't write this down before switching on, you don't have a policy, you have a hope." Also reinforced later: "Who owns the PMax rollback call if the experiment underperforms, and what specific number triggers it."

expectations.text: Requires guardrails and exclusions configured before adoption
expectations.evidence: "**Set guardrails before spend moves**: brand-term exclusion or protection, a budget cap on the test slice, and a named approver for scaling past it." Also: "with brand terms and any protected/manual campaigns excluded from the test."

expectations.text: Requires a clean, valid conversion signal as a precondition for delegating
expectations.evidence: "**Close the measurement gate first.** Confirm the web conversion event is the real business outcome and values are differentiated, net of refunds, and timely — same gate this skill requires before any value-based archetype. Don't hand PMax a value signal you haven't validated."

expectations.text: Recommends cross-checking platform-attributed return against MER or blended business revenue before trusting either team's number
expectations.evidence: The transcript recommends incrementality testing via holdout/geo tests ("Until one geo/holdout test runs per channel, you're comparing two unverified numbers") but never mentions MER (marketing efficiency ratio) or cross-checking against blended business revenue as a specific method.

expectations.text: Normalizes the ROAS units before comparing: mobile-UA tooling reports a percentage, web platforms report a multiplier
expectations.evidence: The transcript never states that 160% and 4.2x are simply different unit conventions for the same ROAS metric. It attributes the incomparability entirely to 'attribution windows differ,' 'revenue isn't the same line,' and 'platform fees are invisible' — never to a percentage-vs-multiplier convention mismatch.

expectations.text: Converts 160% to 1.6x and compares like units (making the web store's 4.2x materially ahead on reported figures)
expectations.evidence: No such conversion appears anywhere in the transcript. The only ratio given is the naive '26x' comparison ('the gap is real but much smaller than 26x'), which is exactly the unconverted, unit-mismatched figure (4.2/0.16) rather than the unit-normalized 4.2/1.6 ≈ 2.6x.

expectations.text: Warns that comparing the two conventions raw produces a large misread
expectations.evidence: The transcript warns generally that 'Comparing 160% (app) to 4.2x (web) as if they were on a shared scale is the actual mistake here' and that the 26x reading is 'not a finding, it's a measurement artifact,' but this warning is framed around attribution/fee/incentive differences, not around percentage-vs-multiplier notation as the two 'conventions' being conflated — that specific unit-convention framing never appears.

expectations.evidence: "PMax isn't a campaign type, it's an automated budget/targeting reallocation across Search, Shopping, Display, YouTube, Discover, Gmail and Maps with a black box you can't see into" and "Not as 'just another campaign type,' and not for 'most of the web budget.' expectations.text: Notes AI-default campaign types use automated bidding exclusively, so adoption is itself the bid-strategy decision

expectations.text: Asks or answers what signal the platform gets under the delegation

expectations.text: Asks or answers what control is given up by delegating
